adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Nitroprusside can release cyanide. Cyanide blocks terminal electron transfer to O2 at cytochrome c oxidase, stopping oxidative phosphorylation and causing anaerobic lactate production despite oxygen availability.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Prolonged sodium nitroprusside can also cause thiocyanate toxicity, especially with impaired renal clearance, but severe rapidly progressive lactic acidosis despite adequate arterial oxygenation is the classic histotoxic-hypoxia pattern of cyanide. Cyanide's direct mitochondrial target is cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV).
